## Purpose

This is the Next.js App Router tree: it owns the root HTML shell, fonts, and global providers
([layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx)), and every routable URL in the product — auth, dashboard, admin, workflow
launch/run, and handoff. Every page here is a thin entrypoint that authenticates via
`localStorage` token + `getToken()` and then delegates the real UI to `components/`;
**nothing else in the frontend imports from `app`** (`imported_by: []` — it is a leaf the
router mounts, not a library other modules build on).

## Shape

- [layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx) — root layout (server component): loads Manrope + Heebo fonts, sets
  `<html>`/`<body>`, mounts `SkillsHooksProvider` then `RunConnectionProvider` above
  `{children}` so the app-level SSE run stream survives route changes.

- `page.tsx` — `/`, server component, immediate `redirect("/login")`.

- [login/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx) — `/login`, client, email/password form, routes to `/admin` or
  `/dashboard` on success.

- [register/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/register/page.tsx) — `/register`, client; self-registration is disabled, kept alive only
  to `redirect("/login")` for old links.

- [admin/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/admin/page.tsx) — `/admin`, client, user-management console (list/search/create/delete
  users, tier dropdown); gates on `getMe().is_admin`, bounces non-admins to `/dashboard` and
  unauthenticated users to `/login`.

- [[...view]/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/%5B...view%5D/page.tsx) — the catch-all route (spec 015-frontend-routing) that IS
  `/dashboard` and every other authenticated URL (`/create/*`, `/runs/{id}/*`, `/workflows/*`,
  `/library/*`, `/settings/*`, `/analytics`, etc.): chat lane + workflow runs + SSE/WS stream
  handling, wrapped in `DashboardLayout`. `parseViewPath` (`@/lib/routes`) parses the URL
  segments into a `ParsedView` discriminated union; `initialMainViewFor` maps that onto
  `DashboardLayout`'s coarser `MainView` union for cold-mount/back-forward sync. A `screen`
  `parseViewPath` doesn't recognize falls through to `{screen:"unknown"}`, which triggers
  `notFound()` below — the single place a bad/stale URL 404s. The `*.source.test.ts` /
  `*.fix201.test.ts` files alongside it are colocated unit tests, not routes.

- [workflow/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/workflow/page.tsx) — `/workflow`, client, standalone agent-pipeline view (`WorkflowView` +
  `AgentLibrary` slide-out).

- [workflow/create/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/workflow/create/page.tsx) — `/workflow/create`, client, the single unified
  deliverable-launch route; reads `?mode=prototype|ppt` and renders `LaunchWizard` inside a
  `Suspense` boundary (required because `useSearchParams` needs one).

- `handoff/[token]/page.tsx` — `/handoff/:token`, client, dynamic segment; thin wrapper that
  hands the token straight to `HandoffWorkflow` (`components/handoff`).

- [handoff/settings/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/handoff/settings/page.tsx) — `/handoff/settings`, client, standalone integrations
  settings page (`IntegrationsCard`); deliberately not under a `/settings` route so the whole
  handoff feature stays one route family.

- [preview-fullscreen/page.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/preview-fullscreen/page.tsx) — `/preview-fullscreen`, client, full-screen App Builder IDE
  opened via `window.open()` from `AppBuilderPreview`; reads the file payload out of
  `sessionStorage` rather than props/query, since the tab is a separate window.

- test-preview/page.tsx — `/test-preview`, client, hardcoded `MOCK_FILES` harness for
  exercising `AppBuilderPreview` in isolation (dev/QA aid, not a product route).

- [admin/admin.reskin.test.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/admin/admin.reskin.test.tsx), [login/login.reskin.test.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/login/login.reskin.test.tsx) — colocated visual-reskin
  regression tests for their sibling pages.

Only `page.tsx` (root) and [layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx) are server components; every actual page is
`"use client"` because each one needs browser APIs on mount (`localStorage` token,
`useRouter`, `sessionStorage`, `window.location`). `RootLayout` is the sole place providers
are mounted — `SkillsHooksProvider` outside, `RunConnectionProvider` inside — so both are
live above every route in the tree, not per-page.

## Why this shape

The route segmentation mirrors the product's top-level nav (dashboard, workflow, admin,
handoff) one folder per surface, so the URL space is self-describing and each page can stay a
thin shell that imports its real implementation from `components/<feature>/`.

Two routes exist purely as redirect shims (`/` -> `/login`, `/register` -> `/login`) rather
than 404s, because old bookmarks/links must resolve somewhere predictable — that's cheaper
than a custom 404 page and keeps auth entry at a single URL. `handoff/[token]` is the one
dynamic segment; it stays a one-line wrapper around `HandoffWorkflow` specifically so the
token-parsing logic lives with the rest of the handoff feature, not duplicated at the route
boundary. `workflow/create` needs a `Suspense` boundary because `useSearchParams()` is the
mechanism chosen to carry the `mode` (prototype vs ppt) — a generic route parameter instead
of a per-workflow route fork, per the project's single-code-path convention.

**The server/client split is minimal by necessity**: this is an authenticated-first app where
almost every route immediately needs `localStorage`/token state, so only the two routes with
no auth-dependent logic (root redirect, root layout) stay server components. The layout is
where the SSE run connection is deliberately hoisted above the router
(`RunConnectionProvider` wraps `{children}` in [layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx), not in dashboard/page.tsx) —
that keeps a per-run stream alive across client-side navigations instead of being torn down
and reconnected on every route change.
